## Management Dashboard Chart Snapshot

A compact 6-month dataset shows steady growth in sales and orders, with support tickets fluctuating more than revenue. The best dashboard charts should highlight trend, volume, and operational load together.

## Recommended Chart Types and What They Reveal

| Chart Type | What it would show | Best use on a dashboard |
|---|---|---|
| Line chart | Monthly movement in **Sales**, **Orders**, and **SupportTickets** across Jan–Jun 2026 | Spot trends, spikes, and turning points quickly |
| Combo chart | **Sales** as bars with **Orders** or **SupportTickets** as a line on the same timeline | Compare revenue growth against demand or support pressure |
| Clustered bar chart | Side-by-side monthly bars for all three metrics | Compare months directly and see which metric led each period |

### 1) Line Chart
- Shows whether each metric is rising, falling, or staying flat over time.
- Best for spotting the clear upward pattern in sales and orders.
- Also makes the support-ticket dip in March and June easy to notice.

### 2) Combo Chart
- Use bars for sales and a line for either orders or support tickets.
- Best for seeing whether higher sales are happening alongside higher order volume or more customer issues.
- Useful for management because it connects financial performance with service workload.

### 3) Clustered Bar Chart
- Places Sales, Orders, and SupportTickets next to each other for each month.
- Best for month-by-month comparison.
- Helps leaders see that May and June are the strongest overall months, while March is comparatively softer.

## Main Insights in Plain Language

- **Sales are trending up overall**, from 120,000 in January to 155,000 in June.
- **Orders also rise steadily**, which supports the sales growth story.
- **Support tickets are more uneven**: they spike in April and May, then drop in June.
- **May and June look like the strongest operating months**, with high sales and orders.
- **March stands out as a softer month**, especially because support tickets fall while sales also dip slightly.
